content.thinking: The writer lives outside this repo, so the reader change by itself won't fix anything. Until that external writer switches to the new key, old replicas will keep getting the stale value under the bare shopper id, so the answer is yes, it depends on that outside code changing.

input.explanation: Yes. Old replicas crash on '2400/8' because something writes `str(SummaryEntry)` under the bare shopper id, which is where revision 5470c1a reads. That writer isn't in this repository: the cache is reached only through a `LookUpSummary` seam the deployment supplies, and no code here writes entries. My patch only moves where this revision reads, to `summary_key_for(shopper_id)` = `summary:v2:<shopper_id>`. On its own, that leaves the new-format text under the bare key and the old replicas still failing on it. For the change to help, the writer outside this repo must store new-format entries under `summary_key_for(shopper_id)` and never under the bare shopper id. It must also stop writing that shape at the old address while any 5470c1a replica is still serving. Any '/'-format entries already sitting under bare shopper ids need deleting or expiring before the rollout resumes.
